body.text: DOJ has told a federal court that lawful self-defense carry is allowed in public national-park buildings, but the Park Service's own guidance still says it is not.

In a 2 October motion to dismiss in Zimmerman v. Blanche, DOJ argues visitors carrying lawfully for self-defense in park facilities open to the public face no credible threat of prosecution. It is a litigation position, not a ruling, and the NPS page still lists visitor centers as prohibited.
